inputs.text: Thousands of people seeking legal status in immigration court were arrested and detained instead. Court documents reportedly show prosecutors acknowledged the May memo did not authorize those arrests, even as ICE lawyers allegedly invoked it to defend them. This is bigger than a dispute over paperwork: when people face detention for showing up to seek legal protection, the courts themselves can become part of an enforcement system that punishes vulnerability and chills access to due process. We need accountability and safeguards so seeking protection is never turned into a trap.
